title: Pointed clopen refinement along an integral morphism
statement: Let f:X\to Y be an integral morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let \Omega be an algebraically closed field, let y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y, and let t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X satisfy f\circ t=y [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. For every pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v) of t [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], there are a pointed etale neighbourhood (U,u) of y, disjoint open subschemes P,Q of U\times_Y X [def-pc-fibre-product] whose union is U\times_Y X, a geometric point p of P mapping to (u,t), and an X-morphism a:P\to V taking p to v. In particular P is open and closed.

source.place: Proof, integral algebra over the strict henselisation and conservativity

proof.text: Work over an affine neighbourhood of the image of the marked point, then over its strict henselisation A. The base-changed integral algebra B is the directed union of its finite A-subalgebras. Restrict the given pointed etale neighbourhood to a standard etale affine; its finite presentation descends to an etale scheme over one finite subalgebra B_0, preserving the marked geometric point by restriction of its ring map to the descended coefficients.

Decompose B_0 into finite henselian local A-algebras. Their residue fields are finite algebraic extensions of the separably closed residue field of A, hence purely inseparable and separably closed. Thus the factors are strictly henselian. Select the factor determined by the geometric point. The etale neighbourhood over it has a residue-rational point, and henselian etale retraction gives a section through that point. Pull this section and the factor idempotent back from B_0 to B.

The idempotent and its complement cut Spec B into disjoint opens P and Q. Descend the idempotent, its equations, and the section to a pointed etale neighbourhood c of the original base point: the idempotent equations are finite, and both the clopen pieces and the restricted etale neighbourhood are of finite presentation over the corresponding base-changed affine source. Finite-data descent gives their morphism and its equations at one stage. Evaluate the descended section on the geometric point to get p; its composites to the original neighbourhood and to the base-changed neighbourhood give exactly v and (u,t).

lean.statement: theorem exists_pointed_clopen_refinement {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (t : Scheme.Hom.GeometricFiber f y) (V : X.Etale) (v : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber.obj V) : ∃ (c : Scheme.Hom.Nbhd y) (P Q : (pullback c.1.hom f).Opens), Disjoint P Q ∧ P ⊔ Q = ⊤ ∧ ∃ (p : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber.obj (openObj f c P)) (a : openObj f c P ⟶ V), (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber.map a p = v ∧ (Scheme.pointSmallEtale t.1).fiber.map (openIncl f c P) p = ((AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.baseChangeNbhd f y t).obj c).2
